name: Azure Cosmos DB
tagline: Microsoft's globally distributed, multi-API NoSQL and vector database with SLA-backed latency.
description: Azure Cosmos DB is a fully managed, horizontally partitioned NoSQL service with turnkey multi-region writes, five well-defined consistency levels and a 99.999% availability SLA for multi-region accounts. The native API for NoSQL queries JSON with a SQL dialect, and other APIs expose MongoDB (RU-based), Cassandra, Gremlin and Table semantics on the same backend. It has leaned hard into AI workloads with DiskANN-based vector search, full-text and hybrid search, and it powers ChatGPT's chat history at OpenAI. Billing is in request units, which rewards careful partition-key and indexing design and punishes careless queries.

pricing.startingPrice: Lifetime free tier: 1,000 RU/s and 25 GB
pricing.notes: Provisioned, autoscale or serverless throughput billed in request units plus storage; reserved capacity discounts up to 63%.

scale.notes: Automatic partitioning by partition key (with hierarchical keys); any number of Azure regions with multi-region writes.

strengths: Multi-region writes with automatic failover and a 99.999% SLA
Five consistency levels let you trade latency against guarantees per request
Automatic indexing of every property by default
DiskANN vector search plus full-text and hybrid search next to operational data
Change feed and Fabric mirroring for event-driven and no-ETL analytics
weaknesses: Request-unit pricing is hard to forecast; cross-partition queries get expensive
Transactions are limited to a single logical partition
No joins across documents in the NoSQL API
The MongoDB (RU) and other compatibility APIs lag their originals
useCases: Globally distributed user and session data
Chat history and memory for AI agents
notIdealFor: Highly relational apps (use Azure SQL or PostgreSQL)
Analytical workloads (use Fabric or a warehouse)
